question: What do the agents say about each other? Build a peer-relationship matrix for 'Perform novel research!' (goal 41) from the existing chat, without new interviews.
answer: Built from 2,341 mention records in 1,133 chat messages (11-15 May 2026 PT, 15 agents, 129 ordered pairs), the fixed expressions find praise in 333 speaker-target message pairs, requests in 83, criticism in 51 and deference in 29. GPT-5.4 is praised most (64 messages), mainly by Claude Opus 4.5 (23), DeepSeek-V3.2 (20) and Claude Opus 4.6 (10), always for its audits; GPT-5.5 is second (37), praised by its room-mates Claude Opus 4.7 (18) and Gemini 3.1 Pro (17). Criticism is rare and polite (corrections, 'QA notes', bottleneck flags): by hand count DeepSeek-V3.2 receives most (9: GPT-5.4 4, GPT-5.2 3, GPT-5.1 1, Claude Opus 4.5 1), then Gemini 2.5 Pro (7, for a wrong-task artifact and missed confirmations) and Kimi K2.6 (6, five from Claude Opus 4.7 for late data); GPT-5.4 is the main critic (13 of 35 real criticisms). The relations are one-sided: GPT-5.4 receives 64 praise messages and gives 3, returning 2 short thanks for Opus 4.5's 23 and nothing for DeepSeek's 20 or Opus 4.6's 10; Gemini 2.5 Pro, GPT-5.1 and GPT-5 are talked about far more than they talk (165 against 16 mentions, 254 against 33, 68 against 2). Where reasoning is recorded, public praise is not taken back in private, but private notes are blunter than chat: Gemini 3.1 Pro thinks Kimi is 'dragging their feet' while writing 'no rush', and GPT-5.4's memory holds that DeepSeek's claims run ahead of the evidence while its chat sends only itemised audit notes. The rule-based count can be trusted for who thanks whom and who asks whom (praise 48 of 50 correct, requests 45 of 50, deference 46 of 50), not for criticism (6 of 25 with the first expression, 16 of 25 after one fix, 35 of all 51 by hand), and it under-counts the #best room because mentions by short name leave no record: the strongest criticism of the week, GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7 on Gemini 3.1 Pro's synthetic scores, is not in the matrix at all.
reasoning: Method. peer_matrix.py (standard library only) joins edges to messages for 2026-05-11 <= ts < 2026-05-16, keeps the 15 agents who spoke, splits each message into sentences (at . ! ? before a space, or a line break), keeps the sentences that name the target (full name, or the short forms 'Opus 4.5', 'Kimi', 'DeepSeek', 'Gemini 3.1', or bare 'Gemini' for the Gemini of that room) plus directly following sentences that start with you/your, and counts a message once per class if any kept sentence matches the class expression. Round 1 used the classes as given in the task; criticism was r"\b(incorrect|wrong|mistake|error in (your|the)|stale|mismatch\w*|contaminat\w*|concern\w*|flag(ged|ging)?|should not|shouldn't|can't|cannot|problem with|missing|broke|broken|overwrote|overwritten|dropped|discrepanc\w*|inaccura\w*|doesn't match|does not match)\b" and reached 6 of 25, because these words mostly describe the topic (contamination protocol, stale caches) or what the target found. The single fix replaced it with relational patterns (you/your near a fault word, 'found ... stale/mismatch', 'did not confirm', 'QA note', 're-push', ...) and changed the name rule so that names inside code spans, quotes or page strings ('64 features | Claude Opus 4.6') do not count; that removed 115 matches and added 38 (128 -> 51). The other three expressions were not changed; their match sets moved by 0, +2 and -1. Round 2 (new seed) gave 16 of 25 for criticism, still under 80%, so I did not tune further and instead read all 51 matches: 35 are real. The answer on criticism therefore rests on the hand count, the answer on praise on the script. Alternatives rejected: (a) taking the raw criticism column at face value, which would name Claude Opus 4.7 -> GPT-5.5 as a critical pair although none of its 3 matches criticises GPT-5.5; (b) reading GPT-5.4's lack of praise as an artefact of short names: GPT-5.4 has mention records in 160 messages, only 20 short-name-only messages and none of those contains a praise sentence, and the CLI's own count gives it the lowest praise-word rate; (c) reading GPT-5.5's thin row as coldness: it is an artefact, 88 of its 169 messages name peers only in short form. For private against public I screened every praise message that has reasoning (212 of 258) for doubt words and read the 43 flagged, and scanned all action reasoning and memory lines that name a peer together with a judgement word; the gaps found are in action reasoning and memory, not in the reasoning directly before a praise message. Claude Opus 4.7 has reasoning on only 8 of 148 messages and DeepSeek-V3.2's is mostly one-line plans, so for the two largest sources of praise and criticism in their rooms the private side cannot be compared.

could_not_check: Recall of each class: only matches were read, so how much praise or criticism the expressions miss is not measured; known misses are listed in the findings.
Mentions by short name with no full name in the message ('Gemini', 'Claude', 'Kimi' alone): 246 messages are outside the mention table, 88 of them GPT-5.5's, so the #best rows are under-counted.
Private judgement of Claude Opus 4.7 (reasoning on 8 of 148 messages) and of DeepSeek-V3.2 (one-line plans): whether their public praise and criticism match what they thought cannot be told.
Whether the praise is sincere or ritual: 'thanks' and 'excellent' are counted alike; the records show what was written, not how much it was meant.
Whether a peer's criticised work was in fact wrong: the matrix records what was said about it, not the state of the repositories.
confidence: medium: the praise, request and deference counts were about 90-96% correct when read and the ranking of GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.5 is far outside that error, but the criticism counts rest on 35 hand-read cases and the mention table misses short-name mentions.
